courses.title: Global Health Governance
courses.description: Contemporary issues and debates in global health governance and effects on health monitoring and outcomes at individual and population levels. Historical patterns of global health, its regulatory framework, principal coordinating mechanisms and emerging challenges, and implications of globalization and international trade policies.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 3101, or permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: HLTH 3101, or permission of the department

courses.title: New Health Technologies
courses.description: Overview of new and emerging health technologies, including medical and assistive devices, diagnostics and screening, genetics, reproduction, tissue regeneration, imaging, and health informatics. Health technology assessment methods and issues. Regulatory, ethical and social implications; considerations in the developing world.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 1000 or HLTH 1001 and third-year standing or higher, or permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: HLTH 1000 or HLTH 1001 and third-year standing or higher, or permission of the department

courses.title: Applied Health Statistics
courses.description: Statistics concepts and procedures used in the analysis of health data; techniques commonly used to analyze data collected from different types of epidemiological and experimental study designs; how to interpret and present statistical findings.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 3201 and STAT 2507 or permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: HLTH 3201 and STAT 2507 or permission of the department

courses.title: Health Program Evaluation Tools and Methods
courses.description: Introduction to concepts, principles and processes of evaluating health care programs and interventions. Methodological tools including needs assessment, project management skills, use of health information management databases. Issues in communication with stakeholders, including change management and decision making.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 2001 and STAT 2507 or permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: HLTH 2001 and STAT 2507 or permission of the department

courses.title: Pandemics and Infectious Disease
courses.description: Factors that influence disease processes, including viruses, bacteria, protozoa, fungi and infectious agents, how these agents come to have the effects that they do in a given individual, how they spread within and how to limit their spread.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 2004 and HLTH 3302 or permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: HLTH 2004 and HLTH 3302 or permission of the department

courses.title: Inflammatory and Endocrine Factors in Diseases
courses.description: Inflammatory and hormonal processes and their relevance to disease states. Immune-related disorders, heart disease and stroke, metabolic syndrome, diabetes, psychiatric conditions, and neurodegenerative disorders. The contribution of psychosocial and genetic factors to diseases.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 3302 or BIOL 4200 or BIOC 4200 or permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: HLTH 3302 or BIOL 4200 or BIOC 4200 or permission of the department

courses.title: Fundamentals in Pharmacology and Toxicology
courses.description: Introduction to pharmacological principles, xenobiotics and their interactions within living systems. Topics include biological mechanisms of action of xenobiotics on macromolecules, cells and their effects on various organ systems. Social, legal and governmental policies will be discussed.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 3303 or permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: HLTH 3303 or permission of the department

courses.title: Host-Pathogen Interactions
courses.description: Advanced cellular and molecular mechanisms governing host-pathogen interactions and their contribution to disease. Exploration of immune signaling and recognition, virulence factors, antimicrobial resistance and research techniques used in this field.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 2004 and HLTH 3302 or permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: HLTH 2004 and HLTH 3302 or permission of the department

courses.title: Maternal and Perinatal Determinants of Health
courses.description: The integrated genetic, physiologic and environmental events occurring in early life that impact pregnancy, fetal/infant development and disease risk throughout the lifecourse, with a focus on the mechanisms driving these events.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 2003 and HLTH 3302 or permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: HLTH 2003 and HLTH 3302 or permission of the department

courses.title: Disabilities and Disorders Related to Sensory Nervous System
courses.description: Congenital and acquired disabilities related to sensory organs and processes, including visual and hearing impairments, vestibular and balance disorders, reflex problems, and others. Interdisciplinary approach to causes, mechanisms, accessibility, accommodations and interventions.
courses.prereqText: Either 1) HLTH 3503 and (BIOL 2005 or BIOL 3305 or BIOL 3306), or 2) NEUR 3206, or 3) permission of the department.

courses.title: Trauma-related Disability and Impairments
courses.description: Biomedical and psychosocial factors associated with trauma-related illnesses, stressors, injuries and disabilities, including traumatic brain injury, spinal cord injury, fractures, amputations, burns, post-traumatic stress disorder, and others. Short- and long-term considerations for care and rehabilitation.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 3503 and (BIOL 2005 or BIOL 3305 or BIOL 3306) or permission of the department.

courses.description: Introduction to environmental and occupational health; detection, assessment, management and mitigation of chemical, physical and biological hazards.
courses.prereqText: HLTH 3104 or permission of the department.

courses.title: Knowledge Translation
courses.description: The application of knowledge translation in the formulation of policy and the development of skills required to maximize the impact of scientific findings through real world programs and policies and communication skills for diverse audiences.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing and permission of the Department of Health Science and permission of the instructor.

courses.description: Independent study, open to third- and fourth-year students to explore a particular health related topic, in consultation with a Faculty supervisor. May include directed reading, written assignments, tutorials, laboratory or field work.
courses.prereqText: third- or fourth-year standing in the B.H.Sc. program, in addition to permission of the Faculty supervisor and the Department of Health Sciences.

courses.description: Independent critical review and research proposal on a health- related topic, using library, database and/or bioinformatics resources, under the supervision of the course instructor. Seminar topics include identification and critical review of resources, development of scientific writing skills, and formulation of health science-related research.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing in the B.H.Sc. Honours and permission of the Department of Health Sciences.

courses.description: A collaborative project on a health related topic. Students, working together as a team, will complete a research project and develop communication and research skills under the supervision of the faculty supervisor. Evaluation will be based on a written report and oral presentation.

courses.title: Introduction to Human Rights
courses.description: Human rights from an interdisciplinary perspective. Topics may include the foundations and nature of rights, roots of inequality and oppression, aboriginal rights, racism, women and rights, sexual orientation, state and corporate power, economic exploitation, the environment and rights, warfare, torture, and social movements.

courses.title: Human Rights: Theories and Foundations
courses.description: Historical overview of the theoretical and philosophical approaches underlying the human rights movement and relevant to the normative ideals and aspirations of human rights and to the strategies of their implementation.
courses.prereqText: second-year standing.

prerequisites.text: second-year standing

courses.title: Sexuality, Gender, and Security
courses.description: Historical and contemporary analysis of surveillance, security, and regulation of sexuality, race, class, and gender. Students will critically examine how ‘subversives’ were created through discourse and administrative logics such as policy and law.
courses.prereqText: second year standing or permission from the Institute.

prerequisites.text: second year standing or permission from the Institute

courses.title: Power Relations and Human Rights
courses.description: The study of power from a critical, transnational perspective; the impact on human rights of different forms and modalities of power, including those emanating from the state and corporations and those implicated in socio-economic and other hierarchical relations.
courses.prereqText: second-year standing.

prerequisites.text: second-year standing

courses.title: Human Rights and Sexualities
courses.description: Human rights issues in various cultural contexts concerning sex and/or gender, with attention to sexual minorities such as gay, lesbian, and transgendered persons. Forms of discrimination against sexual minorities and the mechanisms and strategies for redress.
courses.prereqText: second-year standing.

prerequisites.text: second-year standing

courses.title: Political Repression
courses.description: Canada is home-in-exile to many who have faced severe and often life-threatening political repression such as imprisonment, torture, surveillance, population transfer, etc. This course examines the impacts on survivors of political repression, and strategies used to overcome its legacies.
courses.prereqText: second-year standing.

prerequisites.text: second-year standing

courses.title: Social and Political Movements
courses.description: The underlying conditions and developments of historical and contemporary social and political movements; specific social movements such as civil rights or gay rights.
courses.prereqText: second-year standing.

prerequisites.text: second-year standing

courses.title: Special Topics in Human Rights
courses.description: This advanced seminar will cover current and topical issues and/or debates in human rights, and will enable students to engage in focused discussions and analyses of these issues. Topics will vary from year to year.
courses.prereqText: third-year standing.

prerequisites.text: third-year standing

courses.title: Right to the City
courses.description: “The right to the city” as an emerging focus of advocacy and analysis in urban movements for social justice around especially the local and transnational dimensions of the “right to the city” movement.
courses.prereqText: third year standing.

prerequisites.text: third year standing

courses.title: Human Rights and Resistance
courses.description: This course problematizes human rights paradigms and critically examines the limitations of the political within liberal democracies. Bringing together theory and politics, alternative approaches to activism are explored. Topics may include struggles grounded in radical democracy, anti-capitalism, and social justice perspectives.
courses.prereqText: third-year standing.

prerequisites.text: third-year standing

courses.title: Racialization, Racism and Human Rights
courses.description: The forms and effects of systemic race-based human rights abuses. Topics may include immigration and refugee policies and practices, anti-apartheid regimes, racial profiling, the racial politics of "nationhood" and armed conflict, civil rights and resistance movements in differing cultural contexts.
courses.prereqText: third-year standing.

prerequisites.text: third-year standing

courses.title: Culture, Religion, and Women's Human Rights
courses.description: The impact of cultural and religious traditions on gender, race, ethnicity and sexuality. Topics may include debates related to power dynamics, historical issues, geopolitics, and cultural relativism.
courses.prereqText: third-year standing.

prerequisites.text: third-year standing

courses.title: Children's Rights
courses.description: This course examines children’s rights from a range of historical, cultural, and global perspectives. Topics may include the rights for Indigenous children, children with disabilities, female, trans and queer children, children in armed conflict and refugees in Canada and transnational contexts.
courses.prereqText: third-year standing.

prerequisites.text: third-year standing

courses.title: Disability Rights
courses.description: A critical approach to the study of disability rights that explores the intersections of disability with race, sexuality, gender, colonialism, ‘health’, and other discourses.
courses.prereqText: third-year standing.

prerequisites.text: third-year standing

courses.title: Anti-Black Racism
courses.description: The course examines conceptual linkages between race, racism and anti-black racism and how anti-Blackness racial prejudice is rooted in Black people’s experience of enslavement and colonization.

courses.title: Histories of Persecution and Genocide
courses.description: Case studies in persecution and/or genocide in different cultural contexts. The social, political, and legal conditions that have enabled the institutional or state-sanctioned persecution of targeted groups, and the circumstances that had an impact on their decline.
courses.prereqText: third-year standing.

prerequisites.text: third-year standing

courses.title: Social, Economic and Cultural Rights
courses.description: The development of social, economic and cultural rights, including rights to housing, healthcare, education and employment. Topics may include the international geopolitics of the historical tension between these rights and civil and political rights.
courses.prereqText: third-year standing.

prerequisites.text: third-year standing

courses.title: Global Environmental Justice
courses.description: Overview of critical debates on environmental issues from a global social justice perspective. Topics may include corporate mining, food sovereignty, poverty, economic exploitation, Indigenous cosmologies and environmental justice, militarization and environmental degradation, privatization of water and climate change.
courses.prereqText: third-year standing.

prerequisites.text: third-year standing

courses.title: Public Health and Human Rights
courses.description: Through a social-scientific analysis of AIDS, this course explores HIV/AIDS as a case study for understanding the politics of public health. Students will critically interrogate the authority of science and explore avenues for democratizing biomedicine and public health policy in various national and policy contexts.
courses.prereqText: third-year standing.

prerequisites.text: third-year standing

courses.title: Citizenship and Human Rights
courses.description: The relationship between citizenship and human rights; how large groups of people, including non-citizens and refugees, are excluded from entitlements to rights. Why human rights rest on citizenship, and with what implications.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing.

prerequisites.text: fourth-year standing

courses.title: Transgender Human Rights
courses.description: Critical analyses of human rights through an examination of transgender subjectivities. The systemic erasure of trans people within society and the struggles of some activists to normalize trans identities.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing.

prerequisites.text: fourth-year standing

courses.title: Disability and Social Justice
courses.description: An intersectional national/transnational approach to social justice issues such as poverty/exploitation, labour, representation, decolonization, race/racism, sexuality and gender from a critical disability studies perspective.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing in Human Rights or Disability Studies.

prerequisites.text: fourth-year standing in Human Rights or Disability Studies

courses.title: Gender, Citizenship and Social Justice in a Transnational World
courses.description: This seminar critically engages with transnational, gendered, classed, and racialized discursive practices of citizenship, human rights, the geopolitics of knowledge and processes of dehumanization through the lenses of decolonial social justice.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing.

prerequisites.text: fourth-year standing

courses.title: Rights of Refugees and Displaced Persons
courses.description: Contemporary issues concerning the rights of refugees and displaced persons, from social, political, and legal perspectives; Canadian and international dimensions of these issues.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing.

prerequisites.text: fourth-year standing

courses.title: Digital Dis-information and Human Rights
courses.description: The course examines the phenomenon of disinformation or ‘fake news’ in the era of digital technology, its intent and links to structures of power and oppression, and its impacts on human rights and the social justice.

courses.title: Counter-terrorism and Human Rights
courses.description: Examines policies and strategies states and international organizations use to combat global terrorism and the challenges these initiatives pose to the international human rights regime, democratic norms, and social justice.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing.

prerequisites.text: fourth-year standing

courses.title: Global Indigenous Knowledges and Movements
courses.description: Indigenous Peoples contributions to world knowledge through community resistance, social movements and scholarship. How processes of corporate globalization impact Indigenous Peoples lives as an ongoing process of normalizing a reconfigured modern coloniality of power.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing.

prerequisites.text: fourth-year standing

courses.title: Black Health
courses.description: The course examines conceptual linkages between race, racism and anti-black racism and how anti-Blackness racial prejudice is rooted in Black people’s experience of enslavement and colonization.

courses.title: Precarity in Labour and Work
courses.description: This course explores how precarious employment and labour arises; the nature and forms of precariousness; how race, citizenship, gender, religion, and location impact precarity; the link between labor and social movements; and types of political and economic initiatives in response to the deepening precarity.

courses.title: Is Religious Freedom a Human Right?
courses.description: Legal, theoretical, and theological interconnecƟons between religion and human rights. Evaluation of concepts including religious freedom, secularism, public sphere, accommodaƟon and neutrality.Examination of religion and culture, interdependence of legal and religious perspectives, boundaries of religion and state, and religious compulsion. Use of case studies.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing.

courses.title: Practicum Placement in Human Rights I
courses.description: This course provides students with the opportunity to spend one day per week (6-8 hours) working and learning at a human rights-related government, research or advocacy organization. A written report is required at the end of the placement. Graded as Sat/Uns.
courses.prereqText: fourth-year standing in Human Rights or permission of the Institute.

courses.description: Recurring symbols in myth, epic and ritual representing the relation between the sacred and the profane, the origin of the cosmos, the basis of community, and formative human experiences. Primary sources drawn from ancient India and China, Mesopotamia, the Hebrew Bible, and Indigenous cultures.

courses.description: The ideas which animated ancient Greek and Roman civilisation and which influenced later western cultural movements through a reading of literary, historical, and philosophical works. Authors include Homer, Herodotus, Thucydides, the Greek Tragedians, Plato, Vergil, and Cicero.

courses.description: Survey of historical and contemporary issues relating to Indigenous peoples in Canada. Cultural traditions and the social interactions between Indigenous and non-Indigenous societies are approached from an interdisciplinary perspective.

courses.description: This course begins by looking at Creation Stories of different Indigenous peoples and builds to discuss Indigenous worldviews, ways of living, ecological relationships, inter-Indigenous relations and diplomacy among Indigenous peoples. courses.description: An interdisciplinary examination of the history of relations between different Indigenous peoples and settler populations from first meetings to the mid-20th century. Topics vary by year, but may include diplomatic relations, trade, spirituality and religion, military alliances, policy, education.

courses.title: Contemporary Indigenous Studies

In-class exercises, lectures and practical experience help students apply these cataloguing standards.

courses.title: Web Development
courses.description: Introduction to Web development. Combining graphics, text, audio, and video to create Web sites; developing different, major working Web sites on an individual basis and in groups, using valid HTML5, cascading style sheets (CSS3), JavaScript and XML structures.

courses.title: Introduction to Interactive Media Design
courses.description: Introduction to interactive multimedia and design, focused on the production and processes of animation, visual fx, game design and development, web design and development, and user experience/interfaces. Topics include: mark-up languages, design process/problem-solving tools, human-centered design, product development, ethics, and copyright and intellectual property.
courses.prereqText: For students not enrolled in CSIT programs.

prerequisites.text: For students not enrolled in CSIT programs

courses.title: Introduction to Programming and Problem Solving
courses.description: Introduction to basic concepts of procedural programming and algorithm design in C. Topics include: basic variables, functions, operators, program control with iteration and conditionals, I/O operations, text and file processing, structures, arrays, pointers, debugging, algorithmic thinking and pseudocode, computer architecture, operating systems, and libraries.

courses.title: Introduction to Scripting and Problem Solving
courses.description: Introduction to basic concepts of object-oriented scripting and algorithm design in Python. Topics include: basic variables, functions, operators, program control with iteration and conditionals, I/O operations, text and file processing, arrays, tuples, lists, debugging, algorithms and pseudocode, computer architecture, operating systems, and libraries.

courses.title: Multimedia Data Management
courses.description: Issues involving the back-end organization of information focusing on databases and database design, server-side scripting, the structured query language (SQL), digital rights management, and watermarking.
courses.prereqText: ITEC 1400 or ITEC1401 and ITEC 1005 or BIT 1400 and IMD 1005 or IRM 1005.

courses.title: Data Visualization
courses.description: Web-based data visualization techniques and systems. Good design practices for visualization, tools for visualization of data from a variety of fields, and programming of interactive web-based visualizations focusing on JavaScript, CSS, SVG and the D3 library.
courses.prereqText: ITEC 2000 or BIT 2008.

prerequisites.text: ITEC 2000 or BIT 2008

courses.title: Intermediate Programming
courses.description: Introduction to object-oriented programming and algorithm design in C++. Topics include code and data encapsulation using classes and objects, inheritance, polymorphism, object-oriented design, data and code abstraction, program efficiency, user interface objects, event-driven systems, and an introduction to linked-lists and searching.
courses.prereqText: ITEC 1400.

prerequisites.text: ITEC 1400

courses.title: Intermediate Scripting
courses.description: Introduction to advanced object-oriented scripting and algorithm design in Python. Topics include class design and encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, object-oriented design, data and code abstraction, program efficiency, user interface objects, event-driven systems, and an introduction to linked-lists, sorting, and searching.

prerequisites.text: ITEC 1401

courses.title: Immersive Storytelling
courses.description: The craft of digital storytelling, creating compelling online and game-engine packages. Using a variety of narrative formats, interactive tools, and digital content, including blogs and RSS feeds, developing an in-depth story using leading edge technologies and techniques.

courses.title: Dynamics and Physics-Based Animation
courses.description: This course deals with the essentials of physics-based animations and dynamics; topics include basics of animation mechanics, collision detection, particle systems, and dynamic systems (cloth, fluid, and hair).
courses.prereqText: IMD 3002 or equivalent.

prerequisites.text: IMD 3002 or equivalent

courses.title: Rigging and Advanced Character Animation
courses.description: This course covers the elements of rigging and advanced character animation; topics include the basics of forwards/inverse kinematics, controls, and weighting, essentials of human and creature rigging, retargeting, face and body motion capture, and motion studies for advanced keyframe animation.
courses.prereqText: IMD 3002 and IMD 3900 or equivalent.

prerequisites.text: IMD 3002 and IMD 3900 or equivalent

courses.title: Visual Effects and Compositing
courses.description: This course covers the essentials of Visual FX and compositing, topics include camera setups (motion control systems), set issues, match-moving, image-based lighting, chroma-keying and object extraction, colour correction, 2D tracking, and rotoscoping.
courses.prereqText: IMD 3002 or equivalent.

prerequisites.text: IMD 3002 or equivalent

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence for Digital Media
courses.description: This course covers the basics of artificial intelligence in games and animation, including behaviour and crowd systems (e.g. boids, reciprocal velocity obstacles, social forces, agent-based modelling, cellular automata), path finding and route planning, as well as procedural animation systems.
courses.prereqText: BIT 2400 or ITEC 2401 or equivalent.

prerequisites.text: BIT 2400 or ITEC 2401 or equivalent

courses.title: Web Application Frameworks
courses.description: A detailed look at web application frameworks, focusing client and server-side frameworks that enable more advanced user interactions, including configuration, understanding functionality, and develop with them effectively.
courses.prereqText: ITEC 1005 or equivalent.

prerequisites.text: ITEC 1005 or equivalent

courses.title: User Experience Design and Accessibility
courses.description: User experience (UX) of interactive systems, including product and service design, usability and UX research. Emphasis on accessibility, with topics including creating accessible systems for users with a range of abilities, accessibility standards, and validation of designs in a practical context.
courses.prereqText: IMD 3004 or equivalent.

prerequisites.text: IMD 3004 or equivalent

courses.title: Digital Audio and Music
courses.description: Introduces the concepts of digital audio & music specifically how it relates to digital media (games, film, mobile, etc). Topics include, digital audio recording, multitrack production and mixing, foley effects, musical interference and intonations, signal processing for effect, time & spatial variations, and studio recording.

courses.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality
courses.description: Design, development, and evaluation of virtual and augmented reality systems. Topics include VR/AR history, applications, hardware (display and input devices), software, interaction techniques for navigation, selection, manipulation, human factors, and empirical validation. Projects will use modern 3D game engines and VR/AR devices.
courses.prereqText: IMD 2006 and IMD 3002 or equivalent.

prerequisites.text: IMD 2006 and IMD 3002 or equivalent

courses.title: Photo and Non-Photo-Realistic Rendering
courses.description: This course deals with physically-based rendering methods and techniques in the global illumination field; topics include the rendering equation, ray and path tracing, radiosity rendering, photon mapping, final gather methods, materials and shaders, as well taking a look at non-photo-realistic rendering.

courses.title: GPU Programming and Real-Time Rendering
courses.description: This course deals with the programming of the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU); topics include real-time rendering, shaders, and other advanced programming techniques that utilise single-instruction / multiple thread parallel processing units.
courses.prereqText: BIT 2400 or equivalent.

prerequisites.text: BIT 2400 or equivalent

courses.title: Directing and Cinematography for Digital Storytelling
courses.description: This course covers the basics of being a director in a digital storytelling environment, including the basics of direction, dealing with actors, following scripts, and dealing with elements of cinematography; including lighting, cameras, shade, and shadow.

courses.title: Environment and Architectural Modelling
courses.description: The course deals with the creation, development, and use of assets for digital environments; with specific focus on the workflows associated with scene construction and architectural modelling for a variety of real-time and non-real-time systems.

courses.title: Foundations: Journalism in Context
courses.description: This course charts a history of the fourth estate in the West from the invention of the printing press to the ascendance of networked digital communication, focusing on the political, economic and technological contexts that have shaped the news media as institutions and industries.
courses.prereqText: for Journalism Honours students only.

prerequisites.text: for Journalism Honours students only

courses.description: The course introduces students to the concepts, issues and challenges in the contemporary Canadian media environment that will shape their professional role as practicing journalists. It will also provide students with an initial opportunity to practice some basic journalistic skills.
courses.prereqText: for Journalism Honours students only.

courses.description: Journalism’s evolution as community creator and guardian of democracy; its greatest scoops and worst misdeeds. From ancient news-sharing to 21st-century expression in blogs, tweets and investigative masterpieces, this course surveys ethical, political and economic contexts of journalism. Not open to Journalism majors.

courses.title: Delivering Journalism: Innovators v. Imposters
courses.description: Activists, imposters and innovators increasingly crowd in on traditional journalism’s role of presenting reliable news and fair discussion. How is public awareness now shaped – and misshaped – and how must journalism reshape, update and defend its borders to serve communities better?.

courses.description: Introduction to legal studies: concepts, sources, nature and functions of law; historical, cultural and constitutional foundations of Canadian legal system; common and civil law traditions; statutory interpretation; precedent; legal institutions; frameworks for analyzing formal and informal conceptions of law and its role in society.

courses.title: Introduction to Legal Studies 2
courses.description: Introduction to legal rules and theoretical approaches for critically understanding the creation, interpretation and enforcement of those rules; the role of judges, juries, lawyers, and lay persons; adjudication and alternative dispute resolution; relationship of law with social change and justice; challenges of access to justice.

courses.title: Social Justice and Human Rights
courses.description: Theories and practices of law and social justice. Issues examined may include: civil democracy and repression; global governance and the rule of law; democratic movements and social power; human rights instruments, regimes and remedies; armed conflict; and humanitarian intervention.
courses.prereqText: 1.0 credit from LAWS 1001, LAWS 1002, or HUMR 1001 [1.0], or PAPM 1001 and PSCI 2003.

courses.prereqText: LAWS 1001 and LAWS 1002.

courses.description: The concepts employed by the law for creating and enforcing legal obligations between persons within society, including contract, tort, fiduciary obligation and restitution. courses.prereqText: LAWS 1001 and LAWS 1002.

courses.description: The institutional and social production of criminal law in Canada. Processes, personnel, and agencies in the criminal legal system. courses.prereqText: LAWS 1001 and LAWS 1002.

courses.prereqText: i) MATH 1005 or MATH 2404, and ii) MATH 2004 or MATH 2008 or MATH 2009; or permission of the School.

children.text: i) MATH 1005 or MATH 2404, and ii) MATH 2004 or MATH 2008 or MATH 2009

courses.title: Mathematical Modeling and Computational Methods
courses.description: Design and analysis of mathematical models for problems in science. Computational methods, including function evaluation, interpolation, solution of linear equations, root finding, integration, solution of differential equations, Fourier series and Monte Carlo methods.
courses.prereqText: i) MATH 1107 or MATH 1104; ii) MATH 1005 or MATH 2007; and iii) knowledge of a computer language.

children.text: iii) knowledge of a computer language

courses.title: Linear Programming
courses.description: Systems of linear inequalities, formulation of linear programming problems, geometric method, the simplex method, duality theory, complementary slackness, sensitivity analysis, branch-and-bound method and cutting plane method for integer linear programming, applications and extensions.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2152 or MATH 2107, or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 2152 or MATH 2107, or permission of the School

courses.title: Combinatorial Optimization
courses.description: Network flow problems, network simplex method, max-flow min-cut problem, integral polyhedra, minimum-weight spanning tree problem, maximum matching problem, maximum stable set problem, introduction to approximation algorithms.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3801 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3801 or permission of the School

courses.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms I
courses.description: An introduction to the design and analysis of algorithms. Topics include: recurrence relations, sorting and searching, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, NP-completeness.
courses.prereqText: i) one of COMP 2402 or SYSC 2100; and ii) one of COMP 2804 or MATH 3855 or MATH 3825 or COMP 3805.

ii) one of COMP 2804 or MATH 3855 or MATH 3825 or COMP 3805

courses.title: Numerical Analysis (Honours)
courses.description: Elementary discussion of error, polynomial interpolation, quadrature, linear systems of equations and matrix inversion, non-linear equations, difference equations and ordinary differential equations. Implementation of numerical methods using a computer language.
courses.prereqText: i) MATH 2000 with a grade of C- or higher; and ii) MATH 1152 with a grade of C- or higher, or (MATH 1107 or MATH 1104 with a grade of B or higher and permission of the instructor).

prerequisites.text: i) MATH 2000

courses.title: Mathematical Software (Honours)
courses.description: Implementation of numerical methods using numerical software packages. Development of scientific and/or operations research applications using application programming interfaces of numerical or optimization libraries. Functional programming for data analysis and machine learning. Experience working with Python, C++, or Java is essential.
courses.prereqText: A grade of C- or higher in MATH 3806 or COMP 3806.

prerequisites.text: A grade of C- or higher in MATH 3806 or COMP 3806

courses.title: Mathematical Analyses of Games of Chance
courses.description: This course covers mathematics used in the modern casino gaming industry. The topics include probabilities, odds, house advantages, variance and risks, optimal strategies, random walks and gambler's ruin, and gaming revenue estimation. Examples are taken from various games such as Roulette, Blackjack, and Poker.
courses.prereqText: one of STAT 2655, STAT 2605, STAT 2507, STAT 2606, STAT 3502, or MATH 3825 or MATH 3855.

prerequisites.text: one of STAT 2655, STAT 2605, STAT 2507, STAT 2606, STAT 3502, or MATH 3825 or MATH 3855

courses.title: Introduction to Number Theory and Cryptography
courses.description: Congruences, distribution of primes, general cryptographic systems, public key cryptographic systems and authentification using number theory, primality testing and factoring in relation to cryptography, continued fractions and Diophantine equations.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2108 or MATH 3101 or MATH 2100; knowledge of a computer language.

courses.title: Modern Computer Algebra
courses.description: Algorithms for multiplication, division, greatest common divisors and factorization over the integers, finite fields and polynomial rings. Basic tools include modular arithmetic, discrete Fourier transform, Chinese remainder theorem, Newton iteration, and Hensel techniques. Some properties of finite fields and applications to cryptography.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2108 or MATH 3101 or MATH 2100, COMP 1005 or equivalent; or permission of the School.

children.text: MATH 2108 or MATH 3101 or MATH 2100, COMP 1005 or equivalent

courses.title: Discrete Structures and Applications
courses.description: Enumeration: elementary methods, inclusion and exclusion, recurrence relations, generating functions and applications. Graph theory and algorithms: connectivity, planarity, Hamilton paths and Euler trails. Error-correcting codes.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2108 or MATH 3101.

prerequisites.text: MATH 2108 or MATH 3101

courses.title: Discrete Structures and Applications (Honours)
courses.description: Enumeration: inclusion and exclusion, recurrence relations, generating functions and applications. Graph theory: connectivity, planarity, Hamilton paths and Euler trails. Error-correcting codes. Designs and finite geometries. Symmetry and counting.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2100 with a grade of C- or higher; or (MATH 2108 or MATH 3101) with a grade of B or higher.

courses.description: On completion of each work term, the student must submit to the School of Mathematics and Statistics a written report on the work performed. Graded Sat or Uns.

courses.title: Fourier Analysis (Honours)
courses.description: Fourier series, Fourier integrals; introduction to harmonic analysis on locally compact abelian groups, Plancherel Theorem, Pontryagin duality; selected applications.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3001 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3001 or permission of the School

courses.title: Functional Analysis (Honours)
courses.description: Banach spaces and bounded linear operators, Hahn-Banach extension and separation, dual spaces, bounded inverse theorems, uniform boundedness principle, applications. Compact operators.
courses.prereqText: MATH 4007 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 4007 or permission of the School

courses.title: Measure and Integration Theory (Honours)
courses.description: Lebesgue measure and integration on the real line; sigma algebras and measures; integration theory; Lp spaces; Fubini's theorem; decomposition theorems and Radon-Nikodym derivatives.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3001 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3001 or permission of the School

courses.title: Group Representations and Applications (Honours)
courses.description: An introduction to the group representations and character theory, with selected applications.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3106, or a grade of B or higher in MATH 3108.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3106, or a grade of B or higher in MATH 3108

courses.title: Rings and Modules (Honours)
courses.description: Fundamental concepts in rings and modules, structure theorems, applications.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3158 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3158 or permission of the School

courses.title: Group Theory (Honours)
courses.description: Fundamental principles as applied to abelian, nilpotent, solvable, free and finite groups; representations.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3106 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3106 or permission of the School

courses.title: Commutative Algebra (Honours)
courses.description: Fields, including algebraic and transcendental extensions, Galois theory, valuation theory; Noetherian commutative rings, including Noether decomposition theorem and localization.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3158 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3158 or permission of the School

courses.title: Homological Algebra and Category Theory (Honours)
courses.description: Axioms of set theory; categories, functors, natural transformations; free, projective, injective and flat modules; tensor products and homology functors, derived functors; dimension theory.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3158 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3158 or permission of the School

courses.title: Fields and Coding Theory (Honours)
courses.description: Introduction to field theory, emphasizing the structure of finite fields, primitive elements and irreducible polynomials. The influence of computational problems will be considered. Theory and applications of error-correcting codes: algebraic codes, convolution codes, decoding algorithms, and analysis of code performance.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2100, or MATH 3101 or MATH 2108 or equivalent; or permission of the School.

children.text: MATH 2100, or MATH 3101 or MATH 2108 or equivalent

courses.title: Introduction to General Topology (Honours)
courses.description: Topological spaces, maps, subspaces, product and identification topologies, separation axioms, compactness, connectedness.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3001 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3001 or permission of the School

courses.title: Introduction to Algebraic Topology (Honours)
courses.description: An introduction to homotopy theory. Topics include the fundamental group, covering spaces and the classification of two-dimensional manifolds.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3106 and MATH 4205; or permission of the School.

courses.title: Foundations of Geometry (Honours)
courses.description: A study of at least one modern axiom system of Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, embedding of hyperbolic and Euclidean geometries in the projective plane, groups of motions, models of non-Euclidean geometry.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3106 (may be taken concurrently) or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3106 (may be taken concurrently) or permission of the School

courses.title: Introduction to Differentiable Manifolds (Honours)
courses.description: Introduction to differentiable manifolds; Riemannian manifolds; vector fields and parallel transport; geodesics; differential forms on a manifold; covariant derivative; Betti numbers.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3002 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3002 or permission of the School

courses.title: Analytic Number Theory (Honours)
courses.description: Dirichlet series, characters, Zeta-functions, prime number theorem, Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions, binary quadratic forms.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3057 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3057 or permission of the School

courses.title: Algebraic Number Theory (Honours)
courses.description: Algebraic number fields, bases, algebraic integers, integral bases, arithmetic in algebraic number fields, ideal theory, class number.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3158 (may be taken concurrently) or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3158 (may be taken concurrently) or permission of the School

courses.title: Case Studies in Operations Research (Honours)
courses.description: Applications of the principles of Operations Research to practical problems in business, management, and science. Students present at least one case and analyze cases in the published literature. Cases may also be presented by visiting practitioners.
courses.prereqText: STAT 2509 (or STAT 2559) and MATH 3801; or permission of the School.

courses.title: Partial Differential Equations (Honours)
courses.description: First-order partial differential equations. Classification of second-order linear partial differential equations; the diffusion equation, wave equation and Laplace's equation; separation of variables; Fourier and Laplace transform methods for the solution of initial/boundary value problems; Green's functions.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3057 and one of MATH 3008 or MATH 3705, or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3057 and one of MATH 3008 or MATH 3705, or permission of the School

courses.title: Topics in Differential Equations (Honours)
courses.description: Topics in the theory and application of differential equations; for example, hyperbolic systems, fluid dynamics, nonlinear wave equations, optimal mass transport, control theory, calculus of variations.
courses.prereqText: i) MATH 3008; and ii) one of MATH 3001 or MATH 3057; or permission of the School.

children.text: ii) one of MATH 3001 or MATH 3057

courses.title: Dynamical Systems (Honours)
courses.description: Basic concepts of dynamical systems. Vector formulation for systems. Theory of autonomous systems in one, two and higher dimensions. Limit sets, stability. Phase plane, qualitative interpretation, limit cycles and attractors. Parametric dependence, bifurcations and chaos. Applications.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3001 and MATH 3008 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3001 and MATH 3008 or permission of the School

courses.title: Asymptotic Methods of Applied Mathematics (Honours)
courses.description: Asymptotic series: properties, matching, application to differential equations. Asymptotic expansion of integrals: elementary methods, methods of Laplace, stationary phase and steepest descent, Watson’s lemma, Riemann-Lebesgue lemma. Perturbation methods: regular and singular perturbation for differential equations, multiple scale analysis, boundary layer theory, WKB theory.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3057 and at least one of MATH 3008 or MATH 3705, or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3057 and at least one of MATH 3008 or MATH 3705, or permission of the School

children.text: MATH 3057 and at least one of MATH 3008

courses.title: Topics in Combinatorics (Honours)
courses.description: An in-depth study of one or more topics from: generating functions, Polya's theory of counting, block designs, coding theory, partially ordered sets and Ramsey theory.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2100 and MATH 3855 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 2100 and MATH 3855 or permission of the School

courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Logic (Honours)
courses.description: Symbolic logic, propositional and predicate calculi, set theory and model theory, completeness.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2100 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 2100 or permission of the School

courses.title: Computable Functions (Honours)
courses.description: Recursive functions and computability, algorithms, Church's thesis, Turing machines, computational logic, NP-completeness.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2100 or MATH 3855 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 2100 or MATH 3855 or permission of the School

courses.title: Theory of Automata (Honours)
courses.description: Finite automata and regular expressions, properties of regular sets, context-free grammars, pushdown automata, deterministic context-free languages. Turing machines, the Chomsky hierarchy. Undecidability, intractable problems.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3106 or MATH 3158 or MATH 3855 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3106 or MATH 3158 or MATH 3855 or permission of the School

courses.title: Numerical Linear Algebra (Honours)
courses.description: Matrix computations, conditioning/stability, direct methods for linear systems, classical iterative methods: Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel; modern iterative methods, Arnoldi decomposition, GMRES and other Krylov subspace-based methods for sparse and structured matrices; numerical solution of eigenvalue problems, implementation using suitable programming language, application to differential equations/optimization problems.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2152 or MATH 2107; MATH 2000 and MATH 3806; or permission of the School.

courses.title: Game Theory (Honours)
courses.description: One-player games, two-player zero-sum games, multi-player games, games in normal form, games in extensive form, utility theory, Nash equilibrium and Nash arbitration scheme, games in characteristic function form, cooperative solutions, dominations, stable sets, core, Shapley value, applications of game theory.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3801 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3801 or permission of the School

courses.title: Graph Theory and Algorithms (Honours)
courses.description: Paths, circuits, Eulerian and Hamiltonian graphs, connectivity, colouring problems, matching, Ramsey theory, network flows.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3106 or MATH 3158 or MATH 3855 or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3106 or MATH 3158 or MATH 3855 or permission of the School

courses.title: Mathematical Cryptography (Honours)
courses.description: Topics covered include: a general survey of public key cryptography; classical applications of finite fields and number theory; relevant background in geometry and algebraic curves; computational issues concerning elliptic curves; elliptic curve cryptosystems; security issues.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3158, or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3158, or permission of the School

courses.title: Combinatorial Design Theory (Honours)
courses.description: Existence and construction of combinatorial designs: finite geometries, pairwise balanced designs, balanced incomplete block designs, Steiner triple systems, symmetric designs, PBD closure, latin squares, transversal designs, and applications to information theory.
courses.prereqText: MATH 3855, or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 3855, or permission of the School

courses.title: Numerical Analysis for Differential Equations (Honours)
courses.description: Floating point arithmetic; numerical solution of ODEs; finite difference methods for PDEs; stability, accuracy and convergence: von Neumann analysis, CFL condition, Lax Theorem. Finite element methods: boundary value problems and elliptic PDEs. Spectral and pseudo-spectral methods.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2454 and MATH 3806, or permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 2454 and MATH 3806, or permission of the School

courses.title: Quantum Computing (Honours)
courses.description: Space of quantum bits; entanglement. Observables in quantum mechanics. Density matrix and Schmidt decomposition. Quantum cryptography. Classical and quantum logic gates. Quantum Fourier transform. Shor's quantum algorithm for factorization of integers.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2152 (or MATH 2107) with a grade of C+ or better, and permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 2152 (or MATH 2107)

courses.title: Wavelets and Digital Signal Processing (Honours)
courses.description: Lossless compression methods. Discrete Fourier transform and Fourier-based compression methods. JPEG and MPEG. Wavelet analysis. Digital filters and discrete wavelet transform. Daubechies wavelets. Wavelet compression.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2152 (or MATH 2107) with a grade of C+ or better, and permission of the School.

prerequisites.text: MATH 2152 (or MATH 2107)

courses.title: Honours Project (Honours)
courses.description: Consists of a written report on some approved topic or topics in the field of mathematics, together with a short lecture on the report.
courses.prereqText: B.Math.(Honours) students only.

courses.title: Directed Studies (Honours)
courses.prereqText: B.Math.(Honours) students only.

courses.title: Machine Design and Practice
courses.description: The design of mechanical machine elements is studied from theoretical and practical points of view. Topics covered include: design factors, fatigue, and discrete machine elements. Problem analysis emphasizes the application to practical mechanical engineering problems.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 2001 and MAAE 3202.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 2001 and MAAE 3202

courses.title: Biofluid Mechanics
courses.description: Applications of fundamental fluid mechanics to human circulatory and respiratory systems. Basic viscous flow theory including: blood flow in the heart and large arteries, air flow in extra-thoracic (nose-mouth throat) airways and lungs.
courses.prereqText: MATH 2004 and MAAE 2300.

prerequisites.text: MATH 2004 and MAAE 2300

courses.title: Principles of Manufacturing
courses.description: Manufacturing processes, materials. Casting: solidification and heat flow theory, defect formation, casting design. Metal forming: elementary plasticity theory, plastic failure criteria, force and work calculations. Bulk and sheet forming. Joining: heat flow and defect formation, residual stresses. Machining theory and methods. Hardening: diffusion, wear resistance.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 2700.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 2700

courses.title: Biomaterials
courses.description: Materials used in biomedical applications: metals, polymers, ceramics and composites. Material response and degradation. Properties of biologic materials; bone, cartilage, soft tissue. Materials selection for biocompatibility.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 2700.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 2700

courses.title: Mechanical Systems Design
courses.description: Design of mechanical systems: establishing design criteria, conceptual design, design economics, value analysis, synthesis and optimization. Mechanical elements/systems: gear and flexible drive systems, fluid power systems. These elements are utilized in group design projects.
courses.prereqText: MECH 3002 and fourth-year status in Engineering.

prerequisites.text: MECH 3002 and fourth-year status in Engineering

courses.title: Vehicle Engineering I
courses.description: The course emphasizes the engineering and design principles of road transport vehicles. Topics to be covered include: performance characteristics, handling behaviour and ride quality of road vehicles.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 3004 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 3004 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

courses.title: Vehicle Engineering II
courses.description: Engineering and design principles of off-road vehicles and air cushion technology. Topics include: mechanics of vehicle-terrain interaction - terramechanics, performance characteristics of off-road vehicles, steering of tracked vehicles, air cushion systems and their performance, applications of air cushion technology to transportation.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 3004 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 3004 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

courses.title: Biomedical Device Design
courses.description: Medical Devices: the industry and its regulation. Design methodologies. Examination of specific medical devices: surgical equipment, orthopedic devices, rehabilitation engineering, life support, artificial organs. Case studies.
courses.prereqText: MECH 3710, MAAE 3202, and MECH 4210 and fourth-year status in Engineering.

prerequisites.text: MECH 3710, MAAE 3202, and MECH 4210 and fourth-year status in Engineering

courses.title: Mechanics of Deformable Solids
courses.description: Course extends the student's ability in design and stress analysis. Topics include: introductory continuum mechanics, theory of elasticity, stress function approach, Lamé and Mitchell problems, stress concentrations, thermoelasticity and plasticity.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 3202 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 3202 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

children.text: MAAE 3202 and fourth-year status in Engineering

courses.title: Corrosion and Corrosion Control
courses.description: Introduction to corrosion. Corrosion mechanisms. Thermodynamics of corrosion. Electro-chemical kinetics of corrosion. Corrosion: types, prevention, control, testing, monitoring and inspection techniques. Corrosion in specific metals (eg. Fe, Ni, Ti and Al). Corrosion issues in specific industries: power generation and chemical processing industries.
courses.prereqText: Fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: Fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

courses.title: Fatigue and Fracture Analysis
courses.description: Elastic and elasto-plastic fracture mechanics. Fatigue design methods, fatigue crack initiation and growth Paris law and strain-life methods. Fatigue testing, scatter, mean stress effects and notches. Welded and built up structures, real load histories and corrosion fatigue. Damage tolerant design and fracture control plans.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 3202 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 3202 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

children.text: MAAE 3202 and fourth-year status in Engineering

courses.title: Vibration Analysis
courses.description: Free and forced vibrations of one and two degree-of-freedom systems. Vibration measurement and isolation. Numerical methods for multi-degree-of-freedom systems. Modal analysis techniques. Dynamic vibration absorbers. Shaft whirling. Vibration of continuous systems: bars, plates, beams and shafts. Energy methods. Holzer method.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 3004 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 3004 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

courses.title: Introduction to Nuclear Engineering
courses.description: Atomic theory, nuclear physics, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, mass defect, binding energy, nuclides, neutron diffusion and moderation. Reactor theory, kinetics, control. Reactor types, reactor poisoning, xenon oscillations. Reactor materials, corrosion, fuel and fuel cycle. Nuclear medicine. Radiation protection, reactor safety fundamentals.
courses.prereqText: Fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: Fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

courses.title: Nuclear Power Plant Design
courses.description: Elements of design, basic design, and new generation of nuclear reactors. Major systems of CANDU reactor and its safety principles. Balance of Plant Systems. Licensing requirements for design (IAEA, CNSC and USNRC regulations). Analytical/computer codes in safety assessments and design.
courses.prereqText: Fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: Fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

courses.title: Internal Combustion Engines
courses.description: This course explores the design process of an internal combustion engine including: Internal Aerodynamics, Combustion, Rotating and Reciprocating Components, Structures, Control Systems, Manufacturing and Testing Methods. Students will design/optimize an engine component utilizing industry standard Ricardo Wave simulation software.
courses.prereqText: Fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: Fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

courses.title: Biomechanics
courses.description: The biomechanics of biological systems; muscles and movement, nerves and motor control. Measurements of motion, strain and neural signals. The hand and manipulation; locomotion and the leg.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 2101 and fourth-year status in Engineering.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 2101 and fourth-year status in Engineering

courses.title: Fluid Machinery
courses.description: Types of machines. Similarity: performance parameters; characteristics; cavitation. Velocity triangles. Euler equation: impulse and reaction. Radial pumps and compressors: analysis, design and operation. Axial pumps and compressors: cascade and blade-element methods; staging; off-design performance; stall and surge. Axial turbines. Current design practice.
courses.prereqText: (MAAE 3300 or MECH 3310) and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: (MAAE 3300 or MECH 3310) and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

courses.title: Power Plant Analysis
courses.description: Criteria of merit; selection of power plant for transportation and power generation applications; interrelation among mechanical, thermodynamic and aerodynamic design processes; jet propulsion, turbojets and turbofans; alternative proposals for vehicular power plant; combined cycle applications.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 2400 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 2400 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

courses.title: Power Generation Systems
courses.description: Energy sources and resources. Basic elements of power generation. Hydro-electric, fossil-fuel, fissile-fuel power plants. Geothermal, solar and wind power plants. Economic and environmental considerations. Energy storage. Future power needs.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 2300 and MAAE 2400 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

courses.title: Heat Transfer
courses.description: Mechanisms of heat transfer: fundamentals and solutions. Steady and transient conduction: solution and numerical and electrical analog techniques. Convective heat transfer: free and forced convection for laminar and turbulent flows; heat exchangers. Heat transfer between black and grey surfaces, radiation shields, gas radiation, radiation interchange.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 2400 and (MAAE 3300, MECH 3310, or (ENVE 3001 and permission of the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering)) and fourth-year status in Engineering.

courses.title: Heating and Air Conditioning
courses.description: Environmental demands for residential, commercial and industrial systems. Methods of altering and controlling environment. Air distribution. Refrigeration methods, equipment and controls. Integrated year-round air-conditioning and heating systems; heat pumps. Cooling load and air-conditioning calculations. Thermal radiation control. Component matching. System analysis and design.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 2400 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 2400 and fourth-year status in Engineering or by permission of the department

courses.title: Thermofluids and Energy Systems Design
courses.description: Integration of fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, and heat transfer for design of energy conversion systems. Chemical kinetics and mass transfer. Efficient combustion, fuel cells and batteries. Efficient operation and design of engines, power generators, boilers, furnaces, incinerators, and co-generation systems. Emerging energy systems.
courses.prereqText: MAAE 3400 and fourth-year status in Engineering.

prerequisites.text: MAAE 3400 and fourth-year status in Engineering

courses.title: State Space Modeling and Control
